mascot: Piggy Piya — a friendly pink piggy bank with a little coin slot on her back and a jingle in her step

slides.title: Money Helps Us Buy 🛒
slides.text: Money is what we use to buy things! In India our money is the RUPEE. We write it with the symbol ₹. When Meera wants a toffee, she gives the shopkeeper money and the toffee is hers!
slides.spoken: Money helps us buy things. In India our money is the rupee.

slides.title: Meet the Coins 🪙
slides.text: Coins are small, round metal money! Indian coins are ₹1, ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10. The number on the coin tells you how many rupees it is worth. A ₹5 coin is worth 5 rupees!
slides.spoken: Coins are metal money: one, two, five and ten rupees.

slides.title: Meet the Notes 💵
slides.text: Notes are paper money! Indian notes are ₹10, ₹20, ₹50 and ₹100. Notes can be worth MANY rupees, so we keep them flat and safe in a wallet.
slides.spoken: Notes are paper money: ten, twenty, fifty and one hundred rupees.

slides.title: Count Money by Adding 🧮
slides.text: To count money, add the value of each coin! A ₹5 coin and a ₹2 coin: 5 plus 2 makes 7. So you have ₹7. Add every coin to know how much money you have!
slides.spoken: To count money, add each coin's value.

slides.title: Same Money, Different Coins 💡
slides.text: Different coins can make the SAME amount! Five ₹1 coins put together make ₹5 — just like one ₹5 coin. The look is different, but the value is the same!
slides.spoken: Five one-rupee coins make the same money as one five-rupee coin.

challenges.question: Look at the coins. Which coin is worth 5 rupees?
challenges.hint: Find the coin with the number 5 on it!
challenges.misconception: Read the number written on the coin. The ₹5 coin shows 5.

challenges.question: Which one is a NOTE (paper money)?
challenges.hint: Notes are made of paper. Coins are made of metal!
challenges.misconception: ₹2 and ₹5 come as small metal coins. ₹50 comes as a paper note.

challenges.question: Add the coins: ₹2 + ₹2 = ?
challenges.misconception: Two rupees and two more rupees make 4 rupees.

challenges.question: Anu has a ₹5 coin and a ₹2 coin. How much money in all?
challenges.hint: Add: 5 plus 2. Count on from 5: six, seven!

challenges.question: Which coin is worth the MOST money?
challenges.hint: Bigger number on the coin means more money!
challenges.misconception: 10 is the biggest number here, so the ₹10 coin is worth the most.

challenges.question: Drag each money into the right box: is it a coin or a note?
challenges.hint: Coins are metal and round. Notes are paper.
challenges.misconception: ₹1 and ₹2 are metal coins. ₹50 and ₹100 are paper notes.

challenges.question: How many ₹1 coins make ₹10?
challenges.hint: Count ten 1-rupee coins: 1, 2, 3... all the way to 10!
challenges.misconception: Each coin is ₹1, so you need ten of them to make ₹10.

challenges.question: A toffee costs ₹5. Which coin pays for it EXACTLY?
challenges.hint: Exact means just enough — no extra, no less!
challenges.misconception: The ₹5 coin is exactly 5 rupees — perfect for a ₹5 toffee!
